clue.text: Think again about Welshman lagging behind on bend

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece set on another follows it
lagging is insulation wrapped round pipes, so the Welsh name is wrapped round the bottom

parts.note: Rees is a common Welsh surname, standing for any Welshman
behind as a noun is the bottom, colloquially an ass
an S-bend is a bend shaped like the letter S

explanation.surface: A Welshman trailing behind on a bend in the road has second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lagging' looks like falling behind, but here it means wrapping, as pipes are lagged with insulation.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider or evaluate something afresh is to think again about it.

clue.text: "Run about looking lively!" is instruction to players

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: lively means the letters of about bounce into a new order

explanation.surface: A coach shouts at players to run about and look lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests a sports team; they are musicians, and rubato is a direction in a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubato is a musical direction to play with flexible tempo, telling performers how to play.

clue.text: Life on other planets? One's right to start off sceptical

parts.note: one is A, as in a or one apple; the 's is is, a link
a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

indicators.note: to start off means only the opening letter of sceptical is used

explanation.surface: Someone sceptical about life on other planets is told they are entitled to doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: such beings would be life on other planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraterrestrial beings from other worlds would be the life found on other planets.

clue.text: Miss cue on air — sorry!

parts.note: a cue is a sign or signal to act

indicators.note: sorry means in a poor state, so the letters of on air are knocked about

explanation.surface: A broadcaster apologises for missing a cue while on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb; it is the title of a young unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Signorina is Italian for an unmarried young woman, the equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: They're sure out of their minds, these criminals

parts.note: safe means sure, certain, as in a safe bet
crackers is informal for crazy

explanation.surface: Some crooks are so confident they seem mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Safecrackers are thieves who break open safes, a kind of criminal.

clue.text: Foul what detective chief superintendent did

definitions.meaning: foul here means rotten and stinking, as stale butter goes
a chief superintendent heads the CID (Criminal Investigation Department), so read as two words

explanation.surface: A senior police officer's dirty dealings are being described.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten, off-smelling food is called foul or rancid.

clue.text: Unique all-rounder regularly missed

indicators.note: regularly missed means every other letter of all-rounder is skipped

explanation.surface: A unique cricketing all-rounder is sorely missed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alone in its kind, with nothing else like it, is unique.

clue.text: Showing off count's diamonds failed to impress

indicators.note: off means wrong or disordered, so the letters of count are shown jumbled

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A count showing off his diamonds does not impress anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing off' looks like flaunting; 'off' is the anagram signal on COUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut no ice is an idiom meaning to have no effect or influence on someone.

clue.text: Press reduction

definitions.meaning: to press clothes is to take the creases out
a reduction is a lessening, fall or drop

explanation.surface: A newspaper announces a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing removes creases, a joke sense, while a lessening in amount is the plain sense.

clue.text: Stop calling on British — that's to do with success

indicators.note: in an across answer, the phrase set on British comes after it

parts.note: to ring off is to end a telephone call

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop pestering the British, as if that were the key to success.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring off a plan is to achieve it, to carry it through successfully.

clue.text: A lot of credit goes to a writer showing imagination

indicators.note: the shortened word for credit is placed after the writer's name

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

indicators.note: a lot of a word, but not all of it, means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to give someone credit is to tick them off on a list; a tick is also informal for credit

explanation.surface: Most of the praise goes to an author whose work shows imagination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' drops the last letter; buying on tick means buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing that is poetic is imaginative and expressive in the way verse is.

clue.text: Need to go to France, you said? Maybe everyone requires accommodation

indicators.note: everyone needs to be housed inside the rearranged letters
maybe signals that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound as a letter

parts.note: the word you, spoken, is the sound of the letter U
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A traveller to France needs somewhere to stay, as everyone does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' scrambles TO FRANCE plus U (from 'you said'); 'requires accommodation' puts ALL inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism for needing the toilet: nature calls when one needs to go.

clue.text: Cowboy's mate a friend of Dorothy — point taken

indicators.note: the compass point is taken in by the dog's name

parts.note: Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A cowboy's pal is compared to Dorothy's companion, and the point is conceded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A friend of Dorothy' is also an old euphemism for a gay man, a false trail; here it is just the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonto is the Lone Ranger's companion in the Western radio and TV series.

clue.text: Fellow, bird … nothing to stop them? She might have done

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a fellow

indicators.note: the nothing stops up, plugs, the bird's name

parts.note: the erne is the sea eagle, a crossword favourite
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A man and his girl (his bird) with nothing stopping them, until a watchful older woman might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' suggests slang for a girlfriend; it is the erne. The definition refers back: a chaperone might have stopped the couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone was an older woman who accompanied a young lady to prevent improper behaviour with men.

clue.text: Getting frisky with 2 — claims such relationships are unsuitable

indicators.note: frisky means playful and lively, so the letters jump about into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 2 down, ALIENS

explanation.surface: Someone claims that relationships getting frisky with extraterrestrials are a bad idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ALIENS and CLAIMS gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A misalliance is an unsuitable marriage or partnership, so these are relationships that are ill-matched.

clue.text: Recreation ground — men's team hosting United

indicators.note: the rearranged team plays host to United, holding it inside
ground means crushed, so the letters of men's team are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A men's team hosts United at their recreation ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recreation ground' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Recreation' and 'ground' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement is entertainment or pastime, the sense of recreation.

clue.text: Stop fighting egghead in glasses!

parts.note: to stem a flow is to stop it
war is fighting
the head, the first letter, of egg

explanation.surface: An intellectual is urged to stop brawling while wearing spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glasses' suggests spectacles; it means drinking glasses. 'Egghead' gives the first letter of egg, not a brainy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Stemware is the collective term for drinking glasses with stems, such as wine glasses.

clue.text: Ready? Most are told to hurry out

indicators.note: the hurried word lies out, outside, round the shortened are

parts.note: geed up means urged on, told to hurry

indicators.note: most of a word drops its last letter

explanation.surface: Is everyone ready? Most of them are being told to hurry out.
explanation.walkthrough: AR, most of 'are', sits inside GEED UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To be geared up is to be prepared and equipped, ready for action.

clue.text: Issue payments from here

parts.note: issue means offspring, so this is where the children get their money from: their parents

explanation.surface: It reads like a bank's instruction about where payments are issued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like the verb for making payments, but it is the noun meaning children.
explanation.definitionFit: The jokey name for parents as a source of loans and handouts to their grown-up children.

clue.text: Bowler's craft timeless

indicators.note: timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: A cricketer's skill is said to be ageless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler's craft' reads as skill; 'craft' is a boat. A seamer is a cricket bowler who makes the ball deviate off its seam.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a seamer is a type of bowler relying on movement off the ball's seam.

clue.text: High area of mountainside not safe for climbing

indicators.note: for climbing says the hidden letters are read backwards
an area of the phrase means a stretch of letters inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A climber warns that part of a mountainside is not safe to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'High area' left the hidden word without an indicator; 'area of' is that indicator, so the definition is just 'High'. In a down answer, climbing reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned is slang for intoxicated by drugs, which is to be high.

clue.text: Speaker's rejected point about suspensions

indicators.note: the reversed point goes about, around, the speaker
rejected means the word for point is thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: an aim is a point or purpose
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: A speaker has his point rejected in a debate about suspensions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns the point round, and 'about' wraps it round the speaker; the 's is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Moratoria, the plural of moratorium, are temporary suspensions of an activity.

clue.text: School evicting privileged lady from land

indicators.note: evicting means throwing the lady out of the land

parts.note: terrain is land, a stretch of ground
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the most privileged lady

explanation.surface: A school throws out a privileged lady from its grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to teach.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train or instruct them.

clue.text: Happening twice in 1770

indicators.note: the year spoken has two words, and the wanted letters sit inside each of them, so all round them goes

parts.note: the year said in words opens with seventeen

explanation.surface: Something happened twice in the year 1770.
explanation.walkthrough: A hidden word in letters the clue never prints: say 1770 as 'seventeen seventy' and the answer sits inside both words, which is why the clue says 'twice in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A happening is an occurrence, something that takes place.

clue.text: See 18
Crime-fighter flying to each country in turn, initially

indicators.note: the reversed country comes first, before the rest
turned round means the country's letters are read backwards

parts.note: US is the United States
per man means for each person, to each

explanation.surface: A superhero flies to every country in the world, one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In turn' reverses the country and 'initially' puts it first; 'to each' is read as 'per man'.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-book superhero who flies and battles crime in Metropolis.

clue.text: Grow old (gran finally going into home)

parts.note: ex means former, old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the last letter of gran goes into the word for home

parts.note: a pad is slang for someone's home

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of gran

explanation.surface: Grow old, as gran finally goes into a care home.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand is to increase in size, to get bigger.

clue.text: Advised not to go swimming in lake, deep at one end

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit in the lake

parts.note: a mere is a lake

indicators.note: swimming means the letters of not move about fluidly into a new order
one end of deep is its first letter

explanation.surface: Advice not to swim in a lake because one end is deep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To go swimming' scrambles 'not' into NTO; 'at one end' takes the first letter of deep.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mentored is to be guided and advised by someone experienced.
